decisions.reason: As part of a supplement expansion close to the existing portfolio, it has enough strategic fit and prior investment that management is more likely to persist than withdraw.
The firm publicly launched it for pharmacy customers and it supports the announced consumer-health broadening, which favors continued commitment.
Even with somewhat lower initial visibility, it was built into the supplement line and later given its own page, so management is inclined to justify the rollout by keeping it.
This product received especially visible innovation-oriented promotion within the Trivital line, making escalation of commitment particularly likely.
Despite the valsartan problem, a generic prescription product involves meaningful regulatory and manufacturing investment and the setback can be framed as temporary and external.
As a relatively recent OTC launch that extends the pharmacy portfolio, management is likely to give it more time rather than reverse course quickly.
